sources.citation: Krebs, Julia, Eric Harbour, Evie A. Malaia, Ronnie B. Wilbur, Hermann Schwameder & Dietmar Roehm. 2025. Grammatical control of sign language production: EMG and motion capture analysis of adjective intensification in Austrian Sign Language (ÖGS). Frontiers in Language Sciences 4:1632226. doi:10.3389/flang.2025.1632226
sources.note: Experimental (EMG + motion capture) study of adjective intensification in ÖGS. The word 'stress' occurs only in the introduction, as one of Klima & Bellugi's (1979) ASL sign 'modulations' ('adding stress') and in the list of linguistic functions of movement tension ('1. Prosodic stress marking (see Wilbur, 2022)'); there is no statement about where or how stress falls in ÖGS signs or words.

sources.citation: Krebs, Julia, Eric Harbour, Evie A. Malaia, Ronnie B. Wilbur, Julia Martetschläger, Hermann Schwameder & Dietmar Roehm. 2025. Sign language encodes event structure through neuromotor dynamics: motion, muscle, and meaning. Frontiers in Psychology 16:1689676. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1689676
sources.note: ÖGS verb kinematics/EMG; a full-text search for stress/accent: no occurrence of 'stress' or 'prosod'.

sources.citation: Wilbur, Ronnie B. Curriculum Vitae, September 2025 (Purdue)
sources.note: Bibliographic aid: lists all ÖGS work from the Purdue/Salzburg group, including Schalber 2004 Purdue MA thesis 'Phonological Visibility of Event Structure in Austrian Sign Language - A Comparison of ASL and ÖGS', Hunger, Schalber & Wilbur 2000 TISLR poster on modals in the Styrian dialect of ÖGS 'with a particular focus on repetition and pauses', and Wilbur's own ASL stress papers (1987, 1990, 1999) which are about ASL, not ÖGS.

sources.citation: Krebs, Julia, Ronnie B. Wilbur & Evie A. Malaia. 2026. Testing the Event Visibility Hypothesis in Austrian Sign Language (ÖGS). Language and Cognition 18, e14, 1-31. doi:10.1017/langcog.2026.10061
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent: 'stress'/'prominence' absent; 'prosodic' only in reference to Brentari's (1998) Prosodic Model of sign phonology. Nothing on stress.
